title: Sweatman's career and what he asked of Moore
summary: Sweatman was strong in the Twenties, declined afterward, did not sing, and wanted drum solos from Moore.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, I guess we could find out who they are soon enough. So Sweatman's base of operations was pretty much the Lafayette Theatre. Or did he play at other places in New York?

No... He played other small places, you know, like little weddings or something, big weddings... But he didn't do too much. After that, he wasn't doing so hot. Then I think he went to work down at the union, 802, working down there, doing something down there. I don't know what he was doing, but...
Would you say that he was an entertainer as much as he was a musician? He was popular for being able to blow two or three instruments at one time?

Just three instruments. He wasn't popular. He didn't... That's all. He didn't sing. He didn't showmanship. Just played them horns. There was nobody doing that but him during that time. A number like a ...(?)... A lot of them old-time numbers. "Love Will Find A Way." He played clarinet... He used to play them three horns and play in three-part harmony. He would like keep his own piano (?).
Would you say that he was not... Even though he had this talent, apparently he was not very successful from merely a professional standpoint.
Well, during that time, he was going very strong, before I come to New York. That's what I heard. That's like in the Twenties.
But later on it changed, apparently.
Yes. See, now, I was kind of lucky(?), by hanging out with the musicians and having all the musicians in there... [INAUDIBLE SENTENCE] I was real young then. I must have been around...
